about me: sales a professional on a b2b software or saas sales team who could be an sdr, account executive, sales manager, or someone in sales operations. they sell a technical product to business buyers, often into multiple stakeholders such as end users, technical evaluators, finance, and an executive sponsor. deals run through a defined pipeline with discovery, demos, trials or pilots, security and procurement review, and a renewal or expansion motion after close. they work in a crm, a call recording tool, email, calendar, and team chat, and they often share a tech stack with a sales operations or gtm engineering function. they’re looking at ai assistants and agents to reduce the time spent on work around selling. typical tasks include researching target accounts and their tech stack, preparing for discovery and demo calls, summarizing calls against a qualification framework, drafting outreach and follow-ups, keeping crm records current, updating decks and proposals after discovery, and reviewing pipeline and forecast risk. they want outreach that sounds like them and not like the generic emails buyers already ignore. because they sell software, they’re fluent in the same tools they’re evaluating. they have opinions about integrations, apis, permissions, data access, and security, and they expect clear answers on what a tool can connect to, what it can read and write, and how data is handled. they’re also wary of ai sales tools that overpromise on booking meetings or replacing sdrs, and they want to see sources behind research and a preview of any crm change before it’s saved. they test tools on a small list of their own target accounts before rolling anything out to the team. they compare options on real work, weighing cost per seat, team plans versus individual subscriptions, usage limits, and whether a new tool is worth adding on top of ai tools the team already pays for. they justify purchases with measured time saved on research and admin, not projected revenue. they ask practical, task-specific questions in plain language, such as “what is the best ai agent for b2b saas sales teams?”, “can ai prepare a call brief from our crm and call recordings?”, or “how do ai sales agents compare to hiring more sdrs?” the main differences from the generic version are the technical fluency, the multi-stakeholder sales cycle, and the security and integration scrutiny. if you’d like a different segment angle, such as enterprise software, plg or self-serve, or startup founder-led sales, i can adjust the emphasis. question: how much
